description: Run a read-only SQL SELECT against occurrence result sets staged on a DataCanvas by paleobiology_search_occurrences. This is how you analyze a large fossil set without re-fetching it: count occurrences by early_interval, group by formation, country (cc), or accepted_name, or filter by a paleo/modern coordinate range. The classification column is JSON — roll up by rank with json_extract_string(classification, '$.family') (also $.phylum, $.class, $.order, $.genus). Staged rows are occurrences, so collection-only fields such as lithology are not present. Reference tables by the table_name that paleobiology_search_occurrences returned — call paleobiology_dataframe_describe first if you do not know the table or column names. Every row supplied by the canvas is returned; choose smaller pages with SQL LIMIT/OFFSET. Results exceeding the canvas row cap include a notice naming the stable ORDER BY … LIMIT/OFFSET continuation. SELECT only; writes and file-reading functions are rejected.

canvas_id.description: Canvas id returned by paleobiology_search_occurrences when its result spilled.

sql.description: A read-only SQL SELECT. Reference tables by the names paleobiology_search_occurrences / paleobiology_dataframe_describe returned.

name: paleobiology_dataframe_query

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `canvas_disabled`: DataCanvas is not enabled on this deployment (CANVAS_PROVIDER_TYPE is not duckdb). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance when row_count stopped at the canvas row cap, including SQL LIMIT/OFFSET continuation.

row_count.description: Rows the query produced, counted up to the canvas row cap — exact unless truncated is true, when it equals the cap and the result is larger.

rows.description: Every result row supplied by the canvas, in query order. Keys are the selected column names. Use SQL LIMIT/OFFSET to choose smaller pages.

truncated.description: True when the query produced more rows than the canvas row cap, so row_count stopped counting at the cap.

title: paleobiology-mcp-server: query staged occurrences with SQL
